I will do mostly what has worked for me before. On 14 mu with only two people in the house, I cannot spread myself too thin. Wheat and maize are my main stomach crops and money crops together, and with well water I do not dare cut fertilizer too much. If I save too much on fertilizer and the yield drops, that loss hurts more than wasting a little. So I will keep most land in the wheat-maize rotation and leave a smaller piece for cotton, because cotton takes more looking after and more spraying. I will put 10 mu into wheat-maize and 4 mu into cotton. For wheat, I will use improved seed because many people around me plant that now and it stands better and yields better than the old seed. I will fertilize before sowing and give one more topdressing when it starts growing strong in spring. After wheat harvest, I will plant summer maize on the same 10 mu. Maize eats fertilizer and water fast, so I will not let it go hungry. Cotton I will keep on the smaller piece, use improved seed, plough it once, water a few times, and spray more because insects on cotton are always troublesome. I do what I have seen work on nearby fields: keep enough base fertilizer in the soil, add more nitrogen for maize, do not be stingy with water when the crop is at a key stage, and spray when pests show up instead of waiting too long.
